clue.text: Prepared for Revolution, pale Louis emerged, so did state ____?

indicators.note: letters made ready to be turned about are set for a rearrangement, so the next three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A history lesson: as France readied itself for revolution, a wan Louis came out and spoke his famous line.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixteen letters of PALE LOUIS EMERGED are rearranged. The blank in the definition is the phrase Louis XV supposedly said.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis XV is reputed to have said 'after me, the flood', shrugging off whatever disaster would follow his reign.

clue.text: Gear a native mountain climbing team try to reassemble

parts.note: a, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per
a native son is one born in a place
an Alp is a mountain
a rope is a party of mountaineers roped together

indicators.note: the letters of the word try are put back together in another order

explanation.surface: Kit for a local climber: the team must re-rope and have another go up the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'to reassemble' works on TRY, giving RTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear means one's belongings, and movable belongings are a legal synonym.

clue.text: Plant that might receive deaf trumpeter's trumpet?

definitions.meaning: a large-leaved plant, such as colocasia, named for its leaf shape

definitions.text: that might receive deaf trumpeter's trumpet?
definitions.meaning: an elephant trumpets, and a deaf one would hold an ear trumpet to its ear

explanation.surface: A puzzling botanical question about a plant and a hard-of-hearing musician's instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Its huge leaves resemble the ears of an elephant, the trumpeting animal, which is where a hearing aid trumpet would go.

clue.text: Employment in quiet exhibition centre

indicators.note: Employment is placed in the word for quiet, so in signals one piece inside the other

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
use means employment, as in 'put to use'

explanation.surface: Someone finds work in a peaceful gallery space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep mum' is British for keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery or collection open to the public is a place where exhibits are shown.

clue.text: Smith and Young, say, with these troubles?

indicators.note: the clue says these letters joined to the abbreviation for with make the names, so that abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: Will Smith and Will Young are both Wills

explanation.surface: A question asking whether actor Will Smith and singer Will Young suffer certain afflictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: W (with) plus the answer gives WILLS. Will Young is a British pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are misfortunes or problems, so the plural noun matches troubles.

clue.text: Probably fish exist as an example

parts.note: id is a variant spelling of ide, a freshwater fish
are means exist, as in 'there are'
say means for example

explanation.surface: A cautious claim that fish exist as a specimen of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedging remark meaning 'I suppose', which is close to likely or presumably.

clue.text: Where keepers go to speak African language

indicators.note: said out loud, the phrase for the keepers' lavatory gives the language name

parts.note: zookeepers would use a zoo loo, a loo being a British toilet

explanation.surface: A question about where zookeepers head off to chat, in a southern African tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for toilet; 'go' is used in the sense of relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Bantu tongue spoken by millions in South Africa.

clue.text: Note: college study breaks at any time can be wasted

parts.note: me is a variant of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale
Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

indicators.note: study breaks into the word for at any time, splitting it

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever
swat is a variant spelling of swot, to study hard
can and loo are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A note warning that a student's time at college can always be frittered away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is American slang for a toilet, as loo is British slang; 'wasted' is slang for crushed or destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a final crushing defeat, as Napoleon did in 1815, is to be wasted in the slang sense of destroyed.

clue.text: See 1
Legal beagle deprived of fine cheese

indicators.note: the lawyer word loses a letter, so deprived of signals taking it away

parts.note: a brief is slang for a barrister or lawyer
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A lawyer who can't afford a nice cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese from the region near Paris, named after that region.

clue.text: Trump quickly agreed legal case insurance for high flier

parts.note: Donald Trump is President, abbreviated Pres
'Sure!' is a quick word of agreement
a suit is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A political story: the President rapidly settles a lawsuit with his insurers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots at great altitude wear a sealed garment that keeps them safe from low air pressure.

clue.text: Red-top's greeting "fiddler" of motoring luxury

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid, a red-top, so Red-top's is Sun's
hi is a greeting
Nero supposedly fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A tabloid hails some swindler as a figure of luxury motoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Red-tops are British tabloids, from their red mastheads.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening panel in a car's top is a comfort feature for drivers on warm days.

clue.text: As Nelson, returning from the Canaries (nothing like northernmost Africa)

definitions.text: As Nelson, returning from the Canaries

parts.note: the letter O looks like a nought, nothing
Africa's northern edge is near the Med, the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Nelson sailing home from the Canary Islands, with an aside about the geography of north Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson lost his right arm in the 1797 attack on Santa Cruz de Tenerife, in the Canaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral had a single upper limb after his injury, so he came home with one limb fewer.

clue.text: Not so stimulating drink was looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for was looking is read from bottom to top

parts.note: faced means looked towards, so was looking

explanation.surface: Someone looked up from a drink that wasn't much of a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with the caffeine removed gives less of a buzz than ordinary coffee.

clue.text: Summer colour? Ruler's left changes for November

indicators.note: the letter for left is swapped for the one for November

parts.note: a sultan is a Muslim ruler; the 's is 'is'
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A ruler's tan fades as the autumn months come.
explanation.definitionFit: A tan is the browning of skin acquired in the warm season, so a colour of summer.

clue.text: Trial for series censoring one story …

indicators.note: censoring cuts something out, here the letter for one

parts.note: a pilot is a trial episode for a TV series
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trial run for a television show has one storyline removed by the censors.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is the storyline or narrative of a piece of fiction.

clue.text: See 2
… particular page oozing unpleasantness

parts.note: icky means sticky and nasty

explanation.surface: A specific page that seems to drip with nastiness, continuing the story of the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fussy and choosy, as a particular eater is.

clue.text: "Tap tap" is represented thus?

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new order, so represented signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A question about how to write the sound of repeated tapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TAP TAP IS are rearranged, and the result is itself a word for tapping sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit-a-pat is a word for a quick light tapping, so its plural renders a series of taps.

clue.text: Cuts reclusive aviator from radio announcement

indicators.note: words in a radio broadcast are heard rather than read, so it signals a sound-alike

parts.note: Howard Hughes was a pioneering aviator who became a famous recluse

explanation.surface: A radio bulletin trims coverage of a shy flier.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop or cut, as with an axe.

clue.text: See 8
Take exception to something

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence at an unnamed matter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means protest; as a noun it means a material thing.

clue.text: Unimportant extra too often overcomplicated

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that some minor add-on is too often made needlessly complex.
explanation.definitionFit: A note at the foot of a page is supplementary and of minor significance.

clue.text: State no longer iron-clad sort of conclusion

indicators.note: the clue word iron-clad is taken away, signalled by no longer

parts.note: a foregone conclusion is one decided in advance
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron; clad says those letters wrap the outside

explanation.surface: A US state is no longer protected by iron, a conclusion of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: F and E are the outer letters of FOREGONE, so taking away iron 'clad' around the outside leaves the state.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a US state in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Somehow repeatedly earn repute, but not as businessperson

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are combined in an unspecified way
the word earn is used twice over

parts.note: as read as A's, the letter A in plural

explanation.surface: Advice to keep earning a good name without acting in a certain way, as a businessperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' takes the two As from EARNEARNREPUTE before the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who starts businesses and takes financial risks to make a profit.

clue.text: To make both ends meet, people will take this further

indicators.note: where the two words meet, the end of one and the start of the next together hold the answer

explanation.surface: A saying about making ends meet and people pressing on with something.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join of 'both ends'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'and next' or 'after that' moves a story along, which is how people continue a narrative.

clue.text: Recycling fruit, Doc helped this family to fight

definitions.text: Doc helped this family to fight

indicators.note: the fruit's first letter cycles round to the end

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A doctor composting fruit while helping a household in a feud.
explanation.walkthrough: Doc Holliday fought alongside the Earp brothers at the OK Corral gunfight.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp and his brothers were the lawmen family Doc Holliday joined in the famous shootout.

clue.text: Just Spooner's vulgar joint

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: low means coarse or vulgar
the knee is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: Simply a crude place to smoke, according to Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of LOW KNEE gives something said like 'own lee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only both mean merely or no more than.

clue.text: Cliff face, safe before my dad's gathering

indicators.note: my dad's ___ becomes the ___ of Pop, which gathers the other words inside it

parts.note: my dad's thing is the thing of Pop, so the phrase wraps round

indicators.note: safe is placed ahead of face in the answer

parts.note: a peter is criminal slang for a safe
pan is slang for face

explanation.surface: A rock face and a safe sitting before a father's crowd of guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a British pop star famous for never seeming to age. 'my dad's X' is rephrased as 'the X of Pop', which is how it can hold the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliff Richard was nicknamed for the boy who never grew up because of his enduringly youthful looks.
